text:
World Taekwondo marked a decade of humanitarian work Wednesday, celebrating its foundation's efforts to bring sporting opportunities to refugee children and young people through taekwondo.
The ceremony at Seoul's Olympic Parktel commemorated the 10th anniversary of the Taekwondo Humanitarian Foundation (THF), which was formally established in April 2016 as an independent international nonprofit organization based in Lausanne, Switzerland.
The event featured a demonstration by the World Taekwondo Performance Team, remarks by WT President Chungwon Choue, a commemorative concert and an exhibition documenting the foundation's activities.
Diplomatic representatives from Croatia, Costa Rica, Uzbekistan, Cambodia, Sri Lanka and Jordan attended the celebration.
The foundation traces its origins to Sept. 21, 2015, when Choue announced plans for a humanitarian organization during an International Day of Peace event at United Nations headquarters in New York.
Its work is guided by World Taekwondo's vision of "World Peace through Taekwondo," using sport to foster confidence, resilience and opportunity among displaced communities.
Over the past decade, THF has conducted programs in Jordan, Rwanda, Türkiye, Djibouti, Kenya, Switzerland, France, Eswatini and Mexico, with its initiative at Jordan's Azraq refugee camp emerging as a flagship project.
One of its most prominent success stories is Yahya Al Ghotany, a Syrian refugee who began practicing taekwondo at Azraq and later represented the IOC Refugee Olympic Team at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, serving as a flag bearer during the Opening Ceremony.
The International Olympic Committee awarded THF the Olympic Cup in November 2023 in recognition of its work supporting refugees through sport.
The foundation has also broadened its activities through partnerships with other sports, developing its refugee-focused festivals into the Hope and Dreams Sports Festival in 2023.
Its third edition, held at Azraq in 2025, featured taekwondo, Baseball5, badminton, basketball and handball.
As it enters its second decade, THF plans to expand international partnerships and humanitarian programs, extending sporting opportunities to more refugees and underserved communities.
